title: Cartier and Weil Divisors Line Bundles and Picard Groups

items.title: Sheaf total quotient rings
items.statement: For a scheme X define the meromorphic sheaf K_X as the sheafification of U↦S(U)^{-1}O_X(U), where S(U) consists of sections that are nonzerodivisors at every stalk of U. The map O_X→K_X is injective. If X is integral, K_X is the constant sheaf with value K(X).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §31.24 Definition 24.1 and §31.26 Lemma 26.3
The Stacks Project, Definition 111.49.1(6)

items.title: Cartier divisor
items.statement: A Cartier divisor on X is a section of K_X^×/O_X^×. Equivalently it is local meromorphic units f_i on an open cover U_i with f_i/f_j∈O_X^× on overlaps. The additive group law multiplies equations; zero has equation 1.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3
The Stacks Project, Exercises, Definition 111.49.1(6)–(8)

items.title: Cartier divisor local equation equivalence
items.statement: The sheaf-quotient sections K_X^×/O_X^× are exactly local equations modulo refinement and multiplication by local regular units.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: Use local lifts of a quotient-sheaf section, refine overlaps until quotient germs agree, then identify equality with unit ratios. Conversely glue the quotient classes and show refinement/unit changes preserve the global section.

items.title: Principal cartier divisor
items.statement: For f∈Γ(X,K_X^×), define the principal Cartier divisor div_C(f) by its global local equation f; the sign convention is positive for a zero and negative for a pole.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Definition 111.49.1(6)-(7), meromorphic functions and Cartier divisors

items.title: Linear equivalence cartier divisors
items.statement: Cartier divisors D,D′ are linearly equivalent when D−D′=div_C(f) for a global meromorphic unit f.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Definition 111.49.1(6)-(7), meromorphic functions and Cartier divisors

items.title: Effective cartier divisor
items.statement: A Cartier divisor is effective when it has local equations in O_X that are nonzerodivisors in every relevant stalk. A unit equation defines the empty effective divisor.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Definition 111.49.1(6)-(7), meromorphic functions and Cartier divisors
The Stacks Project, Effective Cartier divisors, Definition31.14.1 and Lemma31.14.2

items.title: Effective cartier divisor closed immersion
items.statement: Every effective Cartier divisor D on a scheme X determines a closed immersion D↪X whose ideal I_D is locally (f_i) and is invertible; conversely a closed subscheme locally cut out by nonzerodivisors gives such a divisor.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: On affine charts U_i=Spec A_i, the regular equation f_i yields the quotient scheme Spec(A_i/(f_i)); unit ratios identify these quotients on overlaps. Glue the quotient schemes by the published affine-scheme gluing theorem. The ideals (f_i) glue inside O_X and are locally free of rank one by multiplication with f_i. The glued inclusion is a closed immersion on each chart. Conversely trivialize an invertible ideal and use injectivity to recover regular local equations.

items.title: Picard group of a scheme
items.statement: Define Pic(X) as the abelian group of isomorphism classes of invertible O_X-modules under tensor product, with identity [O_X] and inverse [L^vee]. This is the ordinary group, not a representing Picard scheme or Picard functor; no reducedness, Noetherianity, or connectedness hypothesis is imposed.

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea: Foundations of Algebraic Geometry, October 21, 2011 draft, §14.1.G

items.title: Invertible sheaf of cartier divisor
items.statement: For a Cartier divisor D represented by local equations f_i, define O_X(D)|_{U_i}=f_i^{-1}O_{U_i}⊂K_X: these are rational functions g for which f_i g is regular. Thus effective D permits poles, and O_X(−D) is its ideal sheaf.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Definition 111.49.1(6)-(7), meromorphic functions and Cartier divisors
The Stacks Project, Effective Cartier divisors, Definition31.14.1 and Lemma31.14.2
The Stacks Project, Effective Cartier divisors and invertible sheaves, Definition31.15.1

items.title: Cartier divisor sheaf invertible
items.statement: O_X(D) is an invertible sheaf, locally freely generated by f_i^{-1}; on an integral X it is a fractional subsheaf of K(X).

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: Multiplication by f_i identifies f_i^{-1}O with O on each chart. On overlaps f_i/f_j is a unit, so transition maps are units. On an integral scheme the meromorphic sheaf is the constant function field, giving the fractional embedding.

items.title: Cartier divisor addition tensor
items.statement: For Cartier divisors $D,E$ on a scheme $X$ there are canonical isomorphisms $\mathcal O_X(D+E)\cong\mathcal O_X(D)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(E)$ and $\mathcal O_X(-D)\cong\mathcal O_X(D)^{\vee}$, carrying the local generator $(f_ig_i)^{-1}$ to $f_i^{-1}\otimes g_i^{-1}$ and $f_i$ to $\lambda_i$ with $\lambda_i(f_i^{-1})=1$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: On a common trivializing cover send f_i^{-1}⊗g_i^{-1} to (f_i g_i)^{-1}; check unit-transition compatibility and take E=−D for the dual.

items.title: Rational section line bundle
items.statement: For integral X and an invertible sheaf L, a nonzero rational section is a nonzero element of the one-dimensional K(X)-space L_η at the generic point η, equivalently a section of L⊗K_X.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.title: Line bundle rational section cartier divisor
items.statement: On an integral scheme, every rational (nonzero meromorphic) section $s$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ determines a Cartier divisor $\operatorname{div}_C(s)$ with a canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_X(\operatorname{div}_C(s))\cong\mathcal L$ carrying the canonical rational section $1_D$ to $s$; conversely $\operatorname{div}_C(1_D)=D$ for every Cartier divisor $D$, and $\operatorname{div}_C(s)=\operatorname{div}_C(s')$ if and only if there is an isomorphism $\psi:\mathcal L\to\mathcal L'$ with $\psi(s)=s'$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, Lemma 31.26.3 (tag 01X5) and Definition 31.15.1 (tag 0C4S): meromorphic sections over integral schemes and O(D)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 Exercise 15.2.E (rational section and the sheaf O(div s))

items.strategy: Choose local generators e_i of L and write s=f_i e_i in K(X); nonzero f_i have unit ratios because e_i transition by units. The local isomorphism O(div_C(s))→L is g↦g s, hence f_i^{-1}↦e_i and the canonical rational section 1↦s. These maps glue. Reverse using (O(D),1).

items.title: Cartier divisors mod principal to picard
items.statement: Let $X$ be a scheme with group of Cartier divisors $\operatorname{CaDiv}(X)$ and subgroup $\operatorname{Prin}_C(X)$ of principal Cartier divisors. The rule $D\mapsto[\mathcal O_X(D)]$ is a well-defined group homomorphism $\varphi_X:\operatorname{CaDiv}(X)\to\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ with kernel exactly $\operatorname{Prin}_C(X)$; if $X$ is integral then $\varphi_X$ is surjective, so it induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{CaDiv}(X)/\operatorname{Prin}_C(X)\cong\operatorname{Pic}(X)$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §31.15 (Definition 15.1 and Lemma 15.2: effective Cartier divisors and invertible sheaves), §31.27 (Definitions 27.2, 27.7: Weil divisors and the class group) and §31.28 (Definition 28.4 and Lemma 28.6: the Weil divisor class of an invertible module)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §15.4 (line bundles and Weil divisors; Important Observation 15.4.9 and the diagram (15.4.11.1) computing Pic modulo principal divisors)

items.strategy: Tensor compatibility gives the homomorphism. If O(D)≅O, transport 1 to a global meromorphic unit and compare local generators to show D is principal. On integral X, choose a nonzero generic vector in L_η and apply the rational-section theorem for surjectivity.

items.title: Global section effective divisor
items.statement: If a global section $s$ of an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on a scheme $X$ is regular — equivalently, its coefficient in every local trivialization is a nonzerodivisor — then those local equations glue to an effective Cartier divisor $D$, the local isomorphisms on free generators glue to $(\mathcal L,s)\cong(\mathcal O_X(D),1_D)$ with $1_D\mapsto s$, and the vanishing subscheme $Z_D$ is locally cut out by the coefficient of $s$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, Definition 31.15.6 and Lemma 31.15.10 (tags 01WY and 01X0): regular sections of invertible sheaves and the bijection with effective Cartier divisors
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 Exercises 15.3.B-15.3.C and Section 15.6 (canonical sections and effective Cartier divisors)

items.strategy: Trivialize L, write s=f_i e_i with regular nonzerodivisors f_i, and glue the local closed subschemes Spec(A_i/(f_i)) using the effective-Cartier construction. The local O(D) generator f_i^{-1} maps to e_i, carrying its canonical section 1 to s.

items.title: Weil divisor normal noetherian scheme
items.statement: For a Noetherian normal scheme X, a prime divisor is an integral closed subscheme with generic point ξ satisfying dim O_{X,ξ}=1. A Weil divisor is a locally finite integer sum of prime divisors; on an integral X this is the usual group of codimension-one cycles. Under AC the irreducible components are disjoint and open, so the definition applies componentwise.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Ch. 12 §§12.1–12.9
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.title: Order codimension one rational function
items.statement: For a prime divisor Z in a normal Noetherian scheme X with generic point η_Z and a meromorphic unit f∈Γ(X,K_X^×), ord_Z(f) is the normalized DVR valuation of its germ in O_{X,η_Z}. When X is integral, this applies to f∈K(X)^×.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Ch. 12 §§12.1–12.9

items.title: Principal weil divisor locally finite
items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice. On a normal Noetherian scheme X, a meromorphic unit f∈Γ(X,K_X^×) has nonzero orders at only a locally finite family of prime divisors.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §31.25 meromorphic functions; Noetherian case
The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.24–31.27

items.strategy: Assuming DC through the published finite-minimal-primes theorem, shrink around any point to an affine Noetherian chart on which the meromorphic unit has a representative a/b, with a,b nonzerodivisors at every stalk. A height-one prime with nonzero order contains a or b. Such a prime is minimal over (a) or (b): a nonzerodivisor belongs to no minimal prime, and a height-one prime has no other nonzero prime properly below it. The published finite-minimal-primes theorem applied to A/(a) and A/(b) gives finitely many such primes on the chosen chart; these charts establish local finiteness.

items.title: Principal weil divisor and class group
items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice. For a normal Noetherian integral X define div_W(f)=Σ_Z ord_Z(f)[Z] and Cl(X)=Div(X)/{div_W(f): f∈K(X)^×}.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Ch. 12 §§12.1–12.9
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.title: Cartier to weil divisor normal scheme
items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice. Let X be a normal Noetherian scheme and let D be a Cartier divisor on X, represented on an open cover by local equations f_i in K_X(U_i)^x. For every prime divisor Z of X with generic point xi and every index i with xi in U_i, the germ f_{i,xi} is a unit and the value v_xi(f_{i,xi}) is independent of i and of the chosen local-equation datum; the sum cyc(D) = sum_Z v_xi(f_{i,xi})[Z] is a well-defined Weil divisor on X, independent of charts and equations. If X is integral, cyc(div_C(f)) = div_W(f) for every f in K(X)^x.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3
The Stacks Project, Exercises, Definition 111.49.1(6)–(8)

items.strategy: At each prime divisor the local equation has a nonzero germ in the DVR stalk, so its normalized valuation is a well-defined integer; ratios of local equations are units, so the coefficients do not depend on the chart or the datum. Local finiteness of the support is proved chartwise: on a basic affine neighbourhood the local equation is a fraction a/s, and its nonzero order loci have generic points that are minimal primes of the Noetherian quotients B/(a), B/(s) (the only DC use). On integral X a global equation has exactly the principal Weil orders.

items.title: Cartier to weil respects principal and addition
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice. For a normal Noetherian integral scheme $X$ the associated-Weil-divisor map $\operatorname{cyc}:\operatorname{CaDiv}(X)\to\operatorname{Div}(X)$ is additive, $\operatorname{cyc}(\operatorname{div}_C(f))=\operatorname{div}_W(f)$ for every $f\in K(X)^{\times}$, and there is an induced Cartier/Picard class map $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$ carrying $[\mathcal O_X(D)]$ to the class of $\operatorname{cyc}(D)$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §31.27 (Definitions 27.2, 27.7 and Lemmas 27.4, 27.6: Weil divisors and the class group) and §31.28 (Definition 28.4 and Lemma 28.5 with (28.5.1): the class of an invertible module)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §15.4 (line bundles and Weil divisors; the diagram (15.4.11.1) and the map Pic to Cl)

items.strategy: On each height-one DVR, valuation of a product is the sum; principal equations map to principal Weil divisors. Quotient by principal Cartier divisors and use the Cartier-to-Picard identification on integral X.

items.title: Cartier to weil injective normal
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a normal
Noetherian integral scheme
([[def-weil-divisor-normal-noetherian-scheme]], [[def-integral-scheme]]).
Then the canonical homomorphism
$$\operatorname{Pic}(X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cl}(X)$$
of [[lem-cartier-to-weil-respects-principal-and-addition]], which sends the
class $[\mathcal O_X(D)]$ of a Cartier divisor to the class of its associated
Weil divisor $\operatorname{cyc}(D)$
([[thm-cartier-to-weil-divisor-normal-scheme]]), is injective.
Moreover, the Cartier-to-Weil cycle homomorphism itself is injective:
if a Cartier divisor $E$ satisfies $\operatorname{cyc}(E)=0$, then $E=0$.

The Axiom of Choice is used exactly through the normality and $(S_2)$ inputs
[[lem-normal-domain-implies-s-two]],
[[lem-r-one-s-two-intersection-of-height-one-localisations]] and
[[thm-normality-is-local-for-domains]], which assume it, and through the
implication $\mathrm{AC}\Rightarrow\mathrm{DC}$
([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) that makes the
Dependent-Choice suppliers available.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, Lemma 31.28.6 (Tag 0BE8: for normal X the map Pic(X) to Cl(X) is injective) and Definition 31.28.4 (Tag 0BE6)
J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Ch. 12 §§12.1-12.9 (divisors, the class group and the Picard group)

items.strategy: If the Weil class of L is zero, adjust a rational section by a rational function to make all height-one orders zero. On each normal affine trivialization the resulting coefficient and its inverse lie in every height-one localization because those local rings are DVRs. The S2 intersection theorem puts both in the coordinate ring, so the section generates L.

items.title: Locally factorial scheme
items.statement: A scheme X is locally factorial if every stalk O_{X,x} is a UFD. Under AC, if X is Noetherian and each local ring is a normal Noetherian ring, then X is reduced and its integral components are pairwise disjoint and open, so local factoriality is equivalent to local factoriality on each component. No affine-open UFD equivalence or arbitrary non-locally-Noetherian component claim is asserted.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 6 §§6.4.1 and 6.4.4; Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.title: Cartier weil isomorphism locally factorial
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a locally
factorial Noetherian integral scheme ([[def-locally-factorial-scheme]],
[[def-locally-noetherian-and-noetherian-scheme]], [[def-integral-scheme]]).
Then:

1. $X$ is normal ([[def-weil-divisor-normal-noetherian-scheme]]); in
   particular the cycle map
   $\operatorname{cyc}:\operatorname{CaDiv}(X)\to\operatorname{Div}(X)$
   ([[thm-cartier-to-weil-divisor-normal-scheme]]) and the canonical
   homomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$
   ([[lem-cartier-to-weil-respects-principal-and-addition]]) are defined;
2. every prime divisor $Z\subseteq X$
   ([[def-weil-divisor-normal-noetherian-scheme]]) is an effective Cartier
   divisor ([[def-effective-cartier-divisor]]), and its associated Weil
   divisor is $\operatorname{cyc}(D_Z)=[Z]$;
3. every Weil divisor on $X$ is locally Cartier; equivalently the cycle map
   is surjective, so every Weil divisor is the associated Weil divisor
   $\operatorname{cyc}(D)$ of a Cartier divisor $D$ on $X$
   ([[def-cartier-divisor]]). In fact, the cycle map is an isomorphism of
   divisor groups, using its injectivity on normal schemes
   ([[lem-cartier-to-weil-injective-normal]]);
4. the canonical homomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Cl}(X)$
   of (1) is an isomorphism, so
   $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\cong\operatorname{Cl}(X)$
   ([[def-picard-group-scheme]],
   [[def-principal-weil-divisor-and-class-group]],
   [[def-group-isomorphism-and-automorphism]]).

The Axiom of Choice is used exactly through the injectivity input
[[lem-cartier-to-weil-injective-normal]], whose $(S_2)$ suppliers assume it,
and through the implication $\mathrm{AC}\Rightarrow\mathrm{DC}$
([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) that makes the
Dependent-Choice suppliers of the cycle map available; the unique
factorisation arguments of steps 1.1, 2.1 and 2.2 are choice-free.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, Lemma 31.16.7 (tag 0AGA: a codimension-one integral closed subscheme whose local rings are UFDs is an effective Cartier divisor) and Lemma 31.28.7 (tag 0BE9: for UFD local rings Pic(X) is isomorphic to Cl(X))
The Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.120.11 (tag 0AFV: a unique factorisation domain is normal) and Lemma 10.120.6 (tag 0AFT: a height one prime of a UFD is principal)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1-15.3

items.strategy: A UFD is integrally closed: if a reduced fraction a/b satisfies a monic equation, a prime divisor of b divides a^n and hence a, a contradiction. Thus local factoriality gives normality. At a point, a height-one prime in the UFD local ring is generated by a prime element. For a locally finite divisor, multiply finitely many such generators to the prescribed signed exponents, then shrink the neighborhood to exclude any other codimension-one support. This gives a local rational equation. For injectivity, a local rational function with zero valuations at all height-one primes is a unit by unique factorization. The local conclusions glue and descend modulo principal divisors.

items.title: Pullback cartier divisor
items.statement: For f:X→Y and a Cartier divisor D on Y with local meromorphic equations g_i, f^*D is defined when their pullbacks are meromorphic units on X with unit ratios. For effective D it suffices that each pulled-back regular equation remain a nonzerodivisor. Every flat morphism permits pullback of every Cartier divisor, since flatness preserves injectivity of multiplication by local numerators and denominators.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.title: Pullback cartier divisor line bundle
items.statement: When f^*D is defined, O_X(f^*D)≅f^*O_Y(D), with canonical sections matching for effective divisors.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: On an equation chart g_i, both sides are freely generated by the inverse of f^#g_i; check the transition ratios and, in the effective case, the canonical section 1. The condition on equations is needed so inverse generators live in the meromorphic sheaf.

items.title: Degree divisor proper curve
items.statement: Let k be a field. A proper curve over k is an integral k-scheme C whose structure morphism to Spec k is proper and whose underlying topological space has chain dimension one. Define Div(C) to be the free abelian group on closed points; for D=Σ_x n_x[x], set deg_k D=Σ_x n_x[κ(x):k].

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, §§6.3.9 and 20.4.1 (closed-point and divisor degree definitions; §20.4.1 treats nonsingular projective curves)

items.title: Proper normal curve rational function map
items.statement: Assume AC. Let C be a normal proper curve over k with function field K=k(C), and let f∈K^×. If f is algebraic over k, then f and f^{-1} are global units. If f is transcendental, then K/k(f) is finite and the coordinate f defines a finite locally free dominant map C→P^1_k of degree [K:k(f)]. The images of the target chart rings are k[f] and k[f^{-1}]; the finite free coordinate rings of the chart preimages may be larger.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3
The Stacks Project, Exercises, Definition 111.49.1(6)–(8)

items.strategy: First establish trdeg_k K=1 from the chain dimension of C. In the algebraic case, use monic equations and the unique-minimum valuation rule at each closed-point DVR, then use normality, S2, and the height-one intersection to prove f and f^{-1} are global units. In the transcendental case, show K/k(f) is finite; cover C by the regular loci of f and f^{-1}, construct chart maps from sections on those opens, and glue. Prove dominance, properness, and quasi-finiteness by excluding closed source points from the generic fibre; proper plus quasi-finite gives finiteness. On the actual affine chart preimages, the coordinate rings are finite torsion-free modules over k[t] or k[s], hence free of rank [K:k(f)]. The images of the target chart rings are k[f] and k[f^{-1}], while the preimage algebras may be larger. AC remains assumed and is used through the normality, closed-subset, properness, and proper-quasi-finite suppliers.

items.title: Finite flat curve fibre degree
items.statement: Assume AC. Let C be a normal proper integral curve over k with function field K, let f be in K^x transcendental over k, and let phi_f:C->P^1_k be the finite locally free map of degree d=[K:k(f)] with pullback of the chart coordinate t equal to f. Then sum_{x: phi_f(x)=0} ord_x(f)[kappa(x):k] = d and sum_{x: phi_f(x)=infinity} (-ord_x(f))[kappa(x):k] = d.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Morphisms, §29.49 finite locally free morphisms
The Stacks Project, Morphisms, §29.58 universally bounded fibres

items.strategy: Pull back the two rational points 0 and ∞. A finite locally free algebra of rank d has k-vector-space dimension d after base change to either k-point. Decompose each Artinian fiber into local rings. At x the DVR quotient by f or f^{-1} has length ord_x(f) or −ord_x(f), and each residue-field factor contributes [κ(x):k]. Sum the local dimensions.

items.title: Principal divisors on a normal proper curve have degree zero
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, hence also the Axiom of Dependent Choice. For every normal proper integral curve $C/k$ with function field $K=k(C)$ and every $f\in K^{\times}$, the principal Weil divisor $\operatorname{div}_W(f)$ is a finite integral combination of closed points of $C$ and $\deg_k\operatorname{div}_W(f)=\sum_{x\in C\text{ closed}}\operatorname{ord}_x(f)[\kappa(x):k]=0$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Principal divisors and pushforward, §42.18, Lemmas 42.18.1–3
J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Ch. 12 §§12.1–12.9

items.strategy: If f is algebraic over k, the rational-function-map lemma makes it a global unit, so each order is zero. Otherwise its finite locally free P1 map has zero and infinity fibers both of degree d by the fiber-length lemma; the principal divisor is their difference. AC enters through the proper-quasi-finite theorem in the map lemma.

items.title: Degree descends picard curve
items.statement: Assume AC. On a normal proper integral curve C/k, deg_k O_C(D):=deg_k D defines a well-defined group homomorphism Pic(C)→Z.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Principal divisors and pushforward, §42.18, Lemmas 42.18.1–3
The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Ch. 12 §§12.1–12.9

items.strategy: Each local ring of a normal Noetherian curve is a field or DVR and hence a UFD, so every line bundle has a divisor representative. Two representatives differ by a principal divisor; the theorem makes their degrees equal. Addition of divisors gives additivity.

items.title: Divisor support positive negative parts
items.statement: For D=Σ_x n_x[x] on a regular curve define Supp(D)={x:n_x≠0}, D^+=Σ_x max(n_x,0)[x], and D^−=Σ_x max(−n_x,0)[x], so D=D^+−D^− with disjoint supports.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Ch. 12 §§12.1–12.9

items.title: Effective cartier divisor exact sequence
items.statement: For an effective Cartier divisor i:D↪X, there is an exact sequence 0→O_X(−D)→O_X→i_*O_D→0.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: Identify O_X(−D) with the ideal sheaf I_D; on each equation chart the sequence is 0→(f)→O→O/(f)→0. These local exact sequences glue.

items.title: Twist exact sequence effective divisor
items.statement: For an effective Cartier divisor i:D↪X with ideal sheaf I_D and an invertible O_X-module L, the twist L(−D)=L⊗_{O_X}O_X(−D) is invertible and there is a short exact sequence of O_X-modules 0→L(−D)→L→i_*(L|_D)→0, with α the tensor product of the inclusion I_D⊆O_X with id_L and β the tensor product of the quotient O_X→i_*O_D with id_L, composed with the canonical isomorphism L⊗i_*O_D≅i_*(L|_D) constructed in the proof.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: On each trivializing chart for L, tensoring with L identifies with tensoring with O_X, so the preceding local exact sequence stays exact. Its quotient is the restriction L|_D on the same chart; glue these local identifications.

items.title: Weil pullback not automatic
items.statement: An arbitrary morphism need not pull back a Weil divisor: a local equation can vanish identically on the source, and height-one cycles have no unrestricted contravariant pullback.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.title: Regular locally noetherian locally factorial
items.statement: Every regular locally Noetherian scheme is locally factorial by the regular-local-ring UFD theorem. This is a source-recorded orientation fact only; the locally factorial isomorphism above assumes its own UFD hypothesis and does not use this remark.

references.title: The Stacks Project, A regular local ring is a UFD, Lemma 15.123.2

external_dependency.exact_statement: Every regular local ring is a unique factorization domain.
external_dependency.local_proof_attempt: No proof is supplied in this orientation remark; the source gives an induction on dimension using regular quotients, the prime-height-one criterion, and lifting of factorization.
external_dependency.necessity: Only records the common regular-scheme case; no proved item in this pair uses this unproved remark.

items.title: Noetherian open subsets are quasi-compact

references.title: The Stacks Project; elementary local prerequisite for the Step 5b citation repair

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every open subset of a Noetherian topological space is quasi-compact, including the empty open subset.
items.strategy: Direct elementary proof in the item; all supplier hypotheses and Choice uses are explicit.

title: Cartier and Weil Divisors Line Bundles and Picard Groups — Examples

items.title: Divisor rational function projective line
items.statement: On P^1_k with affine coordinate t, div(t²/(t−1))=2[0]−[1]−[∞], with zeros positive and poles negative.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: Use the standard P1 charts Spec k[t] and Spec k[u], u=1/t; these are normal Noetherian by the polynomial UFD and Hilbert-basis suppliers. The functions t, t−1, and u are local uniformizers at 0, 1, and infinity. At infinity f=u^{-1}/(1−u), so the orders are 2, −1, −1 and zero elsewhere.

items.title: Picard projective line preview
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited from the Proj, properness and twisting-sheaf suppliers. Let k be a field and let X = P^1_k be the projective line over k with its twisting sheaves O_X(n). Then X is a normal proper curve over k, the degree of divisors descends to a group homomorphism deg_k: Pic(X) -> Z, and for every integer n one has deg_k O_{P^1_k}(n) = n; this computes the twists without claiming that every line bundle on P^1_k has this form.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §31.15 (regular sections) and §31.27-§31.28 (Weil divisors, class groups and the Cartier-Weil comparison)
The Stacks Project, Constructions of Schemes, §27.10 (Tag 01MM, twisting sheaves) and §27.8 (standard opens of Proj)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1-15.3 (invertible sheaves, twisting sheaves of projective space, effective Cartier divisors)

items.strategy: The section x_0 of O(1) cuts out one k-rational point, so its Cartier divisor has degree one. Tensor compatibility gives degree n for positive and negative n. No classification of all line bundles is used.

items.title: The unit equation defines the empty effective Cartier divisor
items.statement: A unit equation defines the empty effective Cartier divisor and O_X(∅)≅O_X on every scheme X.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30

items.strategy: Use local equation 1, whose ideal is the whole structure sheaf and quotient is zero. The fractional sheaf 1^{-1}O_X equals O_X.

items.title: A locally principal subscheme need not be an effective Cartier divisor
items.statement: The claim that every closed subscheme locally cut out by principal ideals is an effective Cartier divisor is false: for $X=\operatorname{Spec}k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with the nilpotent $\epsilon$, the closed subscheme $V(\epsilon)$ is cut out by the principal ideal $(\epsilon)$, but every generator of $(\epsilon)$ is a zero divisor, so no regular local equation exists and $V(\epsilon)$ is not an effective Cartier divisor.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: Multiplication by ε kills ε≠0 in k[ε]/(ε²), so (ε) is not freely generated by ε and the effective Cartier regularity criterion fails.

items.title: Cartier divisor hyperplane projective space
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the Proj and twisting-sheaf suppliers. For a field $k$, $n\ge1$ and the hyperplane $H=\{x_0=0\}\subseteq\mathbb P^n_k$ cut out by the first coordinate, $H$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $\mathbb P^n_k$ and there is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_k}(H)\cong\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_k}(1)$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §31.15 (Definition 15.1, Lemma 15.2 and Remark 15.11; regular sections of invertible sheaves and effective Cartier divisors)
The Stacks Project, Constructions of Schemes, §27.8 (Tag 01M3, standard opens of Proj) and §27.10 (Tag 01MM, twisting sheaves)
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1-15.3 (invertible sheaves, regular sections and effective Cartier divisors) and Ch. 4.5 (Proj and its standard charts)

items.strategy: On the standard chart D_+(x_i), x_0/x_i is the nonzerodivisor cutting H; the inverse local generators have exactly the O(1) transition functions. Equivalently use the regular global section x_0 of O(1).

items.title: Divisor cusp normalization pullback
items.statement: Let k be a field, A = k[t²,t³] ⊆ k[t] the subalgebra generated by x = t² and y = t³, C = Spec A, and ν: Spec k[t] → C the morphism induced by the inclusion, so that k[t] is the integral closure of A in k(t) and ν is the normalization of the cusp. Let D = V(x) be the effective Cartier divisor cut out by x. Then D is effective Cartier, ν*D is defined and is the effective Cartier divisor on the normal affine line cut out by t², and the equation t² has order 2 at the origin [0] = V(t) and order 0 at every other prime divisor; moreover O(ν*D) ≅ ν*O_C(D) with constant sections corresponding.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: The semigroup ring k[t²,t³] is a domain, so t² is a nonzerodivisor. Its integral closure is k[t]: t satisfies T²−t²=0 and a normal element of k(t) integral over k[t²,t³] is integral over k[t], hence lies there. Pull the equation back to t² in k[t], whose DVR order at t=0 is 2.

items.title: Weil divisor not cartier singular cone
items.statement: Let k be a field with char k ≠ 2, let R = k[x,y,z]/(xy−z²) with vertex m = (x,y,z), and let X = Spec R be the normal quadric cone. Then Z = V(x,z) is a height-one prime divisor of X that is not Cartier at the vertex: there is no open neighbourhood U of m and no Cartier divisor D on U with cyc_U(D) = [Z ∩ U].

references.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3
The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30

items.strategy: Identify the finitely generated k-algebra A with k[u²,uv,v²]=k[u,v]^{±1}: in characteristic ≠2, invariant polynomials have only even-total-degree monomials, all generated by u²,uv,v². Finite-type Noetherianity applies. The multivariable-polynomial UFD supplier makes k[u,v] integrally closed by the reduced-fraction monic-equation argument: a prime of the denominator would divide the numerator. Any element of Frac(A) integral over A is then integral over k[u,v], hence belongs to k[u,v]; it is invariant and so lies in A, proving normality. The prime P=(x,z) is the unique minimal prime over (x), since A/(x)=k[y,z]/(z²); the principal-ideal theorem gives height at most one, and P≠0 gives height one. At the vertex m=(x,y,z), P/mP has independent classes x,z, so P_m is not principal. If Z were Cartier, its local rational equation h would have valuation one at P and zero at every other height-one prime. Normal S2 and the height-one intersection theorem give h∈A_m. For every g∈P_m, the valuations of g/h are nonnegative at P and every other height-one prime, so the same intersection theorem gives g/h∈A_m. Thus P_m=(h), contradicting the two-generator calculation.

items.title: Pulling back the equation of a Weil divisor can give zero
items.statement: The general claim that every morphism of schemes has a Weil-divisor pullback defined by pulling back local equations is false: for the closed-point map $i:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathbb A^1_k$ landing at the origin, the Weil divisor $[0]=V(t)$ has no naive pullback, because the equation $t$ pulls back to the zero section of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k}=k$ and the source $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has no prime divisors, so $\operatorname{Div}(\operatorname{Spec}k)=0$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: The unique local equation t of [0] maps to 0 in k. Multiplication by zero is not injective, so this is not an effective Cartier divisor; the source has no codimension-one point on which to define the expected cycle.

items.title: Principal divisor degree zero p1
items.statement: Assume AC as inherited from projective-space properness. If p,q∈k[t] are coprime monic polynomials of degrees m,n, then on P^1_k the divisor of p(t)/q(t) has finite closed-point terms from p and q and infinity coefficient n−m; its degree is zero.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Principal divisors and pushforward, §42.18, Lemmas 42.18.1–3
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: Use the standard P1 charts Spec k[t] and Spec k[u], u=1/t, normal and Noetherian by the polynomial UFD and Hilbert-basis suppliers. Factor p and q into irreducible polynomials. A factor r of multiplicity a contributes a[r] and weighted degree a deg r. At infinity u=1/t gives order n−m. Summing finite degrees m−n and infinity n−m yields zero directly, without invoking the general degree-zero theorem.

items.title: An effective divisor on a curve is a finite thickened subscheme of degree deg
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, hence also Dependent Choice. On a normal proper integral curve $C/k$, an effective divisor $D=\sum_i n_i[x_i]$ with $n_i\ge0$ determines an effective Cartier divisor whose associated closed subscheme $Z_D\hookrightarrow C$ is finite over $k$, supported on the points with $n_i>0$, and has $k$-length $\dim_k\Gamma(Z_D,\mathcal O_{Z_D})=\sum_i n_i[\kappa(x_i):k]=\deg_k D$.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Divisors, §§31.14–31.30
J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Ch. 12 §§12.1–12.9
Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea, Ch. 15 §§15.1–15.3

items.strategy: At each x_i use the DVR uniformizer π_i and quotient O_{C,x_i}/(π_i^{n_i}) of module length n_i. Its k-vector-space dimension is n_i[κ(x_i):k]. Extend each of the finitely many local equations to a neighborhood and shrink it so that the equation is a unit away from x_i; glue these ideals with the unit ideal off the support. The resulting closed subscheme has finitely many isolated points; its open-and-closed one-point components are affine spectra of the displayed Artinian local quotients, each finite-dimensional over k. Their finite disjoint union is finite over k, and the local dimensions add.
